chapter_title: Concerning the Summons, in which Limb of the Soul it descended to the First Man
chapter_note: The oldest teaching layer is dominant. This chapter is remarkably clean substrate: body-cosmos correspondences (head=First Man, limbs=sons/soul), the Pillar of Glory as cosmic body, the five intellectual faculties (mind, thought, insight, counsel, consideration) as emanations, and cosmic process narrative of gathering/restoration. Both sides of every mapping stay within the cosmic system. Editorial material is confined to the dialogue frame in ¶1-2 (formulaic attribution, citation formula, self-reference). No editorial bridge, no institutional content, no exhortation. Negative editorial fatigue confirms the editorial vocabulary is front-loaded in the framing paragraphs. The body-head analogy in ¶3-5 is genuinely correspondential (mapping physical body structure onto cosmic hierarchy), not mere illustration.

paragraphs.core_text: In which limb of [the liv]i[ng] sou[l] did [the] summons descend to the Man, who exists in the [a]eon?
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue frame 'Once again one of the teachers questioned the enlightener. He says to him:' (formulaic attribution). Removed 'For it is written in the scriptures about the Man that he spread himself through the [...] aeon as to a wooden house' — citation formula ('it is written in the scriptures') is editorial; the oldest teaching layer expounds, it does not cite. The cited content is cosmological but enters this text via a citation act.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The substantive cosmological question ('In which limb of the living soul did the summons descend') defines the teaching topic and belongs to the Persian pedagogical tradition. The citation formula and 'one of the teachers' (institutional vocabulary flagged at 3.64) are editorial framing. Dialogue_frame score of 7.27 confirms the formulaic opening.

paragraphs.core_text: Indeed, the First Man dispersed himself and he [...] limb of the living soul [...] of the living soul; he has [...] he did not know [... ...] but the blessed, glorious Man came [in] secret; in his image; in his shape; in his love; in his holy virgin, she who is the virgin of light, the soul of the father.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'The [enli]ghtener speaks:' (dialogue frame attribution). Removed 'as I have written for you' (self-citation/editorial self-reference to Mani's own writings).
paragraphs.temporal_note: High substrate score (12.86) confirms the cosmological density. The teaching describes the First Man's dispersion and his coming in secret through image, shape, love, and the virgin of light — systematic cosmic-correspondential content mapping the Man's presence through his emanated aspects. The 'virgin of light, the soul of the father' is a cosmic entity identification. Heavy lacunae obscure much of the first half.

paragraphs.core_text: After the fashion of this fleshly body: as the root of all the limbs hang upon the head, so that should one of the person's limbs be cut off, while the head exists he has hope for [...] but if his head should be cut off, the entire body will die and he is lost.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure body-cosmos correspondence: the physical body's head-limb relationship is mapped onto the cosmic hierarchy (First Man as head, soul-limbs as body). This is correspondential teaching where the physical body is the natural expression of the cosmic structure. All scores at 0.0 — no editorial vocabulary whatsoever. The analogy serves the systematic mapping in ¶4-5.

paragraphs.core_text: This is also the case for the Firs[t] Ma[n]. He is the head, while his sons attach to it the limbs [of] his soul. Or, conversely, like the living air, on which all flesh entirely lives as it breathes and [...] therein. His head is placed on the body of the Pillar of Glory in the heights of the universe.
paragraphs.temporal_note: High substrate score (11.67). Two parallel correspondences: (1) First Man = head, sons = limbs — body-cosmos mapping; (2) First Man = living air on which all flesh lives — element-cosmos mapping. Then the Pillar of Glory as the cosmic body with the First Man as its head. All mappings stay within the cosmic system. The Pillar of Glory is a core cosmic-architectural entity.

paragraphs.core_text: [This i]s also the case [for] the father, the blessed Man; as he is like the head that is upon the body and the air that upon the Pillar is set i[n ...] being made strong by his light virgin, [she] who is his soul that he clothes [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the body-cosmos mapping: head upon body, air upon the Pillar, strengthened by the light virgin who is his soul. All cosmic entities. The 'light virgin' = the soul of the First Man is a systematic identification. All register scores at 0.0. Despite lacunae, the correspondential structure is clear.

paragraphs.core_text: [ ... ] t[h]ose [...]: the mind, thought, insight, counsel and c[on]sideration that he produced and sent forth from hi[m to] do his will. He sprang and travelled behind them. [...] of his living soul, which is entwined among the rebels; as they are like the limbs of its body, and [...] universe.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Highest substrate score in the chapter (20.75). Enumerates the five intellectual faculties — mind, thought, insight, counsel, consideration — which are the five sons/emanations of the First Man in their intellectual aspect. This is systematic emanation-hierarchy teaching. 'Produced and sent forth' is emanation vocabulary. 'Entwined among the rebels' describes the cosmic mixture. 'Like the limbs of its body' continues the body-cosmos correspondence.

paragraphs.core_text: And when they were sent, at [that ti]m[e] he was found with the Virgin of [Lig]ht and [he] stood up, asking and entreating for a p[o]wer. [ ... he] gave him peace and a ki[ss ...] he [gave] him goo[d] tidings [...] Man. The Man him[s]elf gave [his ...] his limbs and gathered his soul i[n ...] he built it in its place like this tower [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic process narrative: the sending of the faculties, the First Man with the Virgin of Light, receiving power, gathering the soul, building like a tower. All cosmic events within the system. 'Built it in its place like this tower' — architectural cosmic metaphor for the Pillar of Glory / Last Statue. All scores at 0.0.

paragraphs.core_text: [...] shaped it and beautified it skillfully [...] for[m ...] the voices that he sent [...] he might sink in and quench [... ...] so[u]l that was crushed by the enemy. They were gathered in. They came, set firm once more, in the image of their father.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Concludes the cosmic process narrative: shaping/beautifying (cosmic craftsmanship), voices sent (the summons), soul crushed by the enemy (Darkness) being gathered and restored 'in the image of their father' (the First Man). Both sides of every mapping remain within the cosmic system. Clean closing to the teaching with no exhortation or editorial overlay. All scores at 0.0.
